answer: We formalize a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds, secured via an opal commitment, enforce a subgame-perfect punishment matrix against adversarial node inflation. Navigating this reef of escalating capital requirements, the expected utility of Sybil multiplication is strictly negative as marginal staked costs exceed the maximum extractable value. These constraints propagate a ripple of deterrent signals forcing Nash equilibrium convergence, where zero-knowledge verifiable delays ensure only authentic resource-heavy actors achieve liveness.
